query: Consider the following context: Temper embrittlement, characterized by a dramatic loss of ductility within a narrow temperature window, is ubiquitous in conventional alloys but is not reported in compositionally complex or high‐entropy alloy systems. In that context, which material can be used for ductile–brittle–ductile transition, and why?

generation.hypothesis: The ductile–brittle–ductile transition can be achieved in high-entropy alloys (HEAs) with specific compositions and microstructures.
generation.material_initial_state: As-cast or annealed HEA with a dual-phase microstructure comprising fcc and hexagonal C14 Laves phases
generation.intervention: High-pressure and high-temperature (HPHT) treatment or introduction of interstitial elements such as O or N
generation.conditions: Room temperature or elevated temperatures up to 1050 °C/1080 °C
generation.structural_mediator: Hierarchically patterned microstructure with coherent interfaces or formation of brittle intermetallic compounds
generation.mechanism: Deformation mechanisms including dislocations, stacking faults, microbands, and deformation twins at multiple length scales, or Snoek-type high-damping behavior due to interstitial relaxation processes
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved strength-ductility synergy, enhanced high-temperature oxidation resistance, or increased wear resistance
generation.baseline: Traditional alloys with limited ductility or high-entropy alloys with single-phase microstructures
generation.boundary: Temperature range, composition, or microstructure of the alloy
generation.uncertainty: Limited generalizability to other alloy systems, uncertainty in the optimal composition or processing conditions for achieving the desired properties

falsification_experiment.design: Systematic variation of composition, processing conditions, and microstructure to evaluate the effects on ductile–brittle–ductile transition
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the alloy exhibits no improvement in strength-ductility synergy or high-temperature oxidation resistance after HPHT treatment or introduction of interstitial elements, the hypothesis is falsified.
